component.name: SDR for Linux
component.summary: Software-defined radio for HPSDR / ANAN transceivers

description.p: A modern GTK4/libadwaita application for HPSDR Protocol 1 and Protocol 2 radios, built on the proven piHPSDR engine and the WDSP DSP library. Full-resolution floating-point panadapter and waterfall, RX demodulation (SSB, CW, AM, digi, RTTY) with low-latency PipeWire audio, and SSB/CW/RTTY transmit with PureSignal linearization.

Includes a TCI server (ExpertSDR3-compatible) for skimmers, loggers and digimode software. Three radios are verified on real hardware by the author — the Apache Labs ANAN G2E, the ANAN 10E/100B and the Hermes Lite 2 (all RX + TX) — and the ANAN G2 (Saturn) had its first live pass from an external tester. Untested models are refused by a safety whitelist, because a wrong relay or filter bit can physically damage a transmitter.

The ANAN G2 (Saturn) graduates to "live-tested": an external operator (W1IZZ) completed two test rounds on his radio — receive probes, per-band PA calibration against an external wattmeter, SWR tracking, a voice QSO, PureSignal correcting with its feedback inside the target window, and the per-model supply-voltage readout confirmed. Still not calibrated by the project itself. From his feedback, the footer supply readout is reworked: a wall-clock exponential average with 0.1 V resolution replaces the flickering hundredths, and the in-band value now follows the theme foreground (the fixed green was unreadable on light themes) with a small margin off the window edge.

A maintenance release built from the first ANAN G2 (Saturn) test report. The three things that run found are fixed: the supply voltage read 0.10 V on the G2 (the Saturn carries it in a different status word — now per model, from piHPSDR and Thetis, still to be confirmed on a G2), there were no band buttons for 60 m and 30 m, and the terminal filled with "DUC sequence errors" lines on the G2 (those status bytes are FIFO telemetry there; the counter is read on the G2E only). For everyone: the transmit-IQ stream start is hardened (no stale packets when the link comes up, live-verified on the G2E), the ANAN 10E no longer shows a supply-voltage number that had no documented source, and the window's minimum width grows by two band buttons. The G2 goes from "unlocked, unproven" to "first live pass done by an external tester — receive probes, per-band PA calibration against an external meter, SWR, a voice QSO — not yet calibrated by us".

Support for the Apache Labs ANAN G2 (Saturn) over HPSDR Protocol 2 — receive, transmit and PureSignal. This model is enabled from an audit of the piHPSDR sources rather than from a test on the hardware, which nobody involved owns: the wire bytes, the wattmeter constants and the PureSignal peak value all come from upstream and are checked by an offline test, but they have never been confirmed against a real G2. It starts safe — power amplifier off, one watt, no stored calibration — so the first transmission belongs into a dummy load. Reports from G2 owners are very welcome. Nothing changes for the ANAN G2E, the ANAN 10E/100B or the Hermes Lite 2.

A native RTTY mode: direct-FSK transmit at 45.45 baud with phase-continuous keying, its own filter presets, an FSK monitor tone and macro keying over TCI. The transmit noise gate is redesigned on one dBFS scale with a visible threshold marker and an adjustable depth — and a long-standing bug that made the gate chop speech (reported as a noisy/distorted monitor) is fixed. The RX S-meter and the TX Mic/Level/ALC meters gained proper ballistics and now read smoothly, the TX monitor no longer stutters at sample rates below 192 kHz, and the application ships a redesigned icon.

Smooth rendering: the spectrum display moves to the GPU. GTK's GL renderer is the default on GTK 4.22 and newer, which collapses frame jitter at 60 FPS, and the waterfall is drawn as a GPU-scaled texture so the application's own frame cost drops to about a millisecond. The About dialog gained a Troubleshooting page with copyable debug info for bug reports, TCI relays spot clicks between clients, and the desktop entry also works for plain source builds. Requires GTK 4.10 or newer.

Two new supported radios: ANAN 10E/100B (Protocol 2, RX+TX) and Hermes Lite 2 (Protocol 1, RX+TX including PureSignal). Contest hardening: CW keying latency cut to ~35 ms, turnaround to ~200 ms, per-mode AGC, mode-aware TX HUD. TX transport hardening on both protocols, TX audio chain controls (mic gain, noise gate, processor), faithful TX monitor, TCI robustness fixes.
First alpha: Protocol 2 RX/TX for the ANAN G2E — panadapter, waterfall, SSB/CW/AM/digi demodulation, SSB and CW transmit, PureSignal, TCI server, band plan overlay, DX spots.
